keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row for it). The page gives no area. The areas transferred under section 12 of the 1803 resolution: the Princely Abbey of Fulda (25 km at Fulda), the Princely Abbey of Corvey (15 km at 9.40E 51.78N), the Free Imperial City of Dortmund (12 km), Weingarten Abbey and the priorate of Hofen (10 km at 9.64E 47.81N) and Dietkirchen Abbey in Nassau (6 km at 8.05E 50.38N). All soft. The Provostry of St. Gerold (Vorarlberg) and the Deanery of Bandern (Liechtenstein) were sold to Austria in 1804 and are not drawn.
New keyframe: 'On 12 July 1806, William Frederick lost the Lordship of Weingarten and the Nassau territories.'

ledger.note: 25 February 1803: the principality. 'The Reichsdeputationshauptschluss resolution on 25 February 1803, legalized the redistribution of the territories'; 'The Prince-Bishopric was secularised and handed to him as a hereditary possession'; created for William Frederick, son of William V of Orange. (On 23 May 1802 France and Prussia had agreed to compensate the Prince of Orange; Prussian troops occupied Fulda on 22 October and William Frederick entered it on 6 December 1802.)

25 February 1803: Corvey. The Princely Abbey of Corvey was among the areas transferred 'under section 12' of the resolution, as one of the four divisions (Fulda, Corvey, Dortmund and Weingarten). The page names no giver other than the resolution.
25 February 1803: Dortmund. The Free Imperial City of Dortmund was among the areas transferred (page names no giver other than the resolution).

ledger.note: 25 February 1803: Weingarten. Weingarten Abbey and the priorate Hofen were among the areas transferred.

region.text: Weingarten Abbey and the priorate of Hofen

ledger.note: 25 February 1803: Dietkirchen. Dietkirchen Abbey (Nassau) was among the areas transferred.
12 July 1806: Weingarten. 'On 12 July 1806, William Frederick lost the Lordship of Weingarten and the Nassau territories'; Weingarten went to the Kingdom of Wurttemberg.
12 July 1806: the Nassau territories, which went to the Grand Duchy of Berg and the Duchy of Nassau (the page does not say which part to which).

27 October 1806: 'Fulda was occupied by French troops on 27 October 1806' after Napoleon defeated Prussia at Jena-Auerstedt (14 October); after William Frederick refused to join the Confederation of the Rhine 'Napoleon took Nassau and Fulda'. The infobox period ends 27 October 1806.

sources.title: Principality of Nassau-Orange-Fulda
sources.note: Established 25 February 1803; Fulda occupied by Prussia 22 October 1802; Weingarten and Nassau lost 12 July 1806; Fulda occupied by France 27 October 1806; Corvey to Westphalia 7 December 1807; Dortmund to Berg 1 March 1808; Fulda to Frankfurt 19 May 1810.

SCOPE. 25 February 1803 to 27 October 1806 (infobox). The four divisions (Fulda, Corvey, Dortmund, Weingarten) appear on the page only as a list; areas, populations and towns are not given.
